title: Chalantika Matri Mandir
subtitle: G+1 Temple with G+3 Guest Block – Architecture, Planning & Structure
description: A twin-sanctum community temple on High Road, Gangarampur: a G+1 main temple crowned by five ribbed shikharas, beside a G+3 guest block for devotees, sadhus and gurus who travel for the puja from across West Bengal and India, with pietra dura inlay and twin approach staircases.
body:
Designed for the Chalantika Mandir Committee on High Road, Gangarampur, Chalantika Matri Mandir brings two sanctums, a congregation space and guest accommodation together on a compact 50' × 50' site. ADS Creative Space prepared the architecture, planning and complete structural design, and the temple is now under construction.

The building is planned in two parts. The main temple is G+1, raised on a podium about 2.5 m above the road, reached by twin staircases and crowned by a cluster of five ribbed shikharas with gilded kalash finials and pietra dura floral inlay. Alongside it, a G+3 guest block hosts the devotees, sadhus and gurus who travel here for the puja from across West Bengal and other parts of India.
features.0.title: A Cluster of Five Shikharas
features.0.text: The G+1 main temple is crowned by a stepped cluster of shikharas: a tall central ribbed shikhara over the sanctums, flanked by four smaller shikharas, each topped with a gilded kalash and banded with gold mouldings. A smaller pavilion with an arched niche faces the street, and the G+3 guest block alongside carries its own stepped golden crown, so the temple reads clearly from High Road.
features.1.title: Raised Temple Floor & Twin Stairs
features.1.text: The temple floor sits on a podium about 2.5 m above the road, giving the sanctum dignity and separating worship from street activity. Two 1.5 m wide staircases rise on either side to a balustraded verandah, so devotees can move up and down at the same time during festivals. Below the podium, a landscaped forecourt and a relief wall with a banyan tree motif welcome visitors at street level.
features.2.title: Pietra Dura Floral Inlay
features.2.text: White marble-finish pillars and walls carry floral inlay in the pietra dura tradition: lilies, leaves and scrolling stems in deep red, green and black. The inlay frames the sanctum fronts and wraps each pillar, giving the white temple warmth and fine detail when seen up close.
features.3.title: Planned for Worship, Gatherings & Pilgrims
features.3.text: The building is planned in two parts. The main temple (G+1) holds two sanctums of about 4.3 × 4.9 m and 4.9 × 4.9 m, separated and surrounded by 1.2 m (4 ft) wide corridors that let devotees move around them, with a congregation and sitting area of about 7.5 × 6.0 m in front; the sanctums rise double-height into the shikharas above. On the left, a G+3 guest block provides rooms on every level, with toilets and a wash area, to host devotees, sadhus and gurus who travel for the puja from across West Bengal and other parts of India.
features.4.title: Elevation, Section & Structure
features.4.text: The drawing set covers the front elevation and a section through the sanctums, setting the podium, floor heights and shikhara proportions. It is backed by a complete RCC structural design: foundation, column, plinth beam, floor beam and slab layouts with schedules and reinforcement details, coordinated with the architecture.
